A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Selective DPO study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the additional Appendix G in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment experiments, difficulty analyses, ablations, and downstream evaluations in Sections 3–6 and Appendices D–F.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds data-selection baseline results and further empirical analyses in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The six-reference-model procedure, held-out validation-loss ranking, easiest-example selection, and sequential DPO training remain unchanged. Appendix A clarifies 'top 50%' as the 50% with lowest validation losses, consistent with v1's main-text procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use UltraChat-200k, UltraFeedback-binarized, Argilla-dpo-mix-7k, the same three alignment benchmarks, and the same six downstream tasks. Appendix G varies ranking criteria, training diagnostics, and reference-model configurations without introducing new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds explicit data-selection competitors: CHES selecting the lowest 50%, RM selecting the highest 50%, and PPL selecting the middle 50%. Figure 12 additionally evaluates perplexity-based ordering, response-length ordering, GPT-4 reward-margin ordering, and Skywork label flipping. These materially broaden comparisons beyond the retained optimization variants and noise-correction baselines.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark protocols and Appendix C configurations remain unchanged. New experiments introduce a two-epoch diagnostic tracking 200 held-out examples in Figure 13 and additional 32B and Mistral reference-model configurations in Figure 14; these supplement rather than replace the earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix G substantially extends the analyses: Figure 12 tests alternative difficulty-ranking criteria, Figure 13 examines stability of preference probabilities during training, and Figure 14 extends curriculum-transfer testing beyond the original 3B-to-7B comparison. Earlier ablations, feature analyses, and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly reports three-run means and dispersion values for the added selection baselines and both Selective DPO variants on AlpacaEval 2. The caption calls the dispersion 'standard variance,' leaving its precise meaning unclear. v1 already reported repeated runs elsewhere; this addition does not establish an increase in runs for retained results.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores remain unchanged, but substantial results are added. For Mistral, Table 1 adds LC/WR values of 18.9/16.6 for CHES, 16.2/13.1 for RM, and 17.3/15.4 for PPL, alongside retained Selective DPO scores of 27.1/28.9. Appendix G adds ranking-comparison curves, mostly stable preference trajectories, and extended curriculum-transfer results. Figure 12 also shows competitive response-length ordering in several settings.

T1.justification: The DPO objective, learned-step and validation-loss definitions, and quantile-based difficulty definition retain their mathematical substance. Figure 13 restates the preference probability implicit in the existing DPO loss. No substantive theorem, assumption, proof, or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: preference difficulty varies, overly difficult examples hinder alignment, difficulty depends on model capacity, and Selective DPO improves AlpacaEval 2 win rates by 9–16% over DPO. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 removes the inference that likelihood and reward-margin results demonstrate more robust reward models and reduced hallucinations. Appendix F softens 'incorrectly labeled' examples to 'likely mislabeled.' Appendix G extends the interpretation of curriculum transfer, while the existing response-length, downstream-mathematics, and RLHF-applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 corrects the Section 3 dataset link from UltraChat-200k to UltraFeedback-binarized. Conversely, Section 6.1 drops v1's explicit ArmoRM attribution for label correction and its label-correctness probability of 0.6 for smoothing. Appendix C's hardware, training, LoRA, and decoding details and the code-access information remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning around CHES and perplexity-based selection, plus references on training dynamics, attention patterns, and self-alignment in Appendix B. These extend the existing framing without replacing its central relationship to prior work. Numerous publication and author-metadata updates concern already cited works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language corrections, condenses explanations, reorganizes the baseline paragraph into three categories, clarifies the pseudocode selection wording, and adds acknowledgements and affiliation details. The main section sequence and most narrative content remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands through Appendix G's multi-panel comparison, training-trajectory heatmap, and extended curriculum plot. Table 1 gains a separate selection-baseline group and uncertainty subscripts. Existing Figures 4–6 are relocated closer to their corresponding discussions; the earlier plots and appendix tables are largely retained.

improvement.justification: Direct selection baselines, Appendix G diagnostics, and uncertainty reporting make the empirical support more informative. Removing the unsupported hallucination inference also improves interpretive restraint. The gains are limited by sparse documentation of the new experiments, ambiguous 'standard variance' terminology, and removal of some baseline implementation details. The core method and existing findings remain unchanged.
